newsitem.title: TURKEY: FORECAST - Turkey Jan inflation seen at 4-5.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Turkey Jan inflation seen at 4-5.3 pct.

text.p: Most bankers expected January Turkish consumer price inflation, due at 0800 GMT on Tuesday, to be between four and 5.3 percent amid an optimistic 1997 economic outlook dominating Turkish markets in recent weeks.
"Our prediction is that January inflation will be below five percent," said Varol Civil, general manager of Bank Kapital.
But a few bankers were more optimistic, forecasting that January inflation could drop as low as three percent.
January price figures are due at 0800 GMT on Tuesday.
In January 1996, consumer prices gained 8.3 percent and wholesale prices jumped 9.8 percent. December 1996 consumer and wholesale inflation data were 3.4 and 3.9 percent, respectively.
Consumer 1996 prices rose 79.8 percent and wholesale prices gained 84.9 percent.
"Markets discounted most of the positive economic expectations, which led to sharp falls in interest rates in January," said an economic research manager of a brokerage.

Bond yields, anticipating tame inflation, have shed some 30 points since late 1996 to 80-81 amid rising liquidity and an increase in withholding tax to 12 percent from 10 percent on interest income from state securities.

But despite positive signs, some bankers warned that recent monetary expansion could put upward pressure on inflation again in coming months. M2 grew 12.8 percent to 2,858 trillion lira ($24.6 billion) from the end of November to January 10, according to central bank data.
Central bank money rose 51 percent to 801 trillion lira from the end of November to January 24.
